code-bollards.title: Bollards: clauses 3.2.2 and 4.2.3.6

intro_cards.title: What this is about
intro_cards.body:
Automated checks of the Code on Accessibility have to settle details that the text does not spell out. These five questions came up when we generated checking rules for clauses 4.7.3.1 and 4.2.3.6 and tested them.

Please answer as you would apply the code. **There is no expected right answer.** "Depends" is a valuable answer: choose it whenever the answer depends on something not stated, and tell us on what.

sections.title: Stair handrails (4.7.3.1)
sections.question: Is this stair in accordance with clause 4.7.3.1(c)?

cards.title: What makes a railing a handrail
cards.prompt: A building model contains railings along a stair. For checking clause 4.7.3.1, what should identify a railing as a stair handrail?

options.label: Its IFC type: IfcRailing with PredefinedType HANDRAIL
options.detail: Other railings are not checked as handrails.

options.label: Any railing that belongs to the stair
A stated property
options.detail: Please name it in the note.

cards.title: Handrail on one side only
changes: The stair has a handrail on ==one side only==.
That handrail is ==continuous== throughout the entire length of the stair and its landings.
There is no handrail on the other side.
cards.hint: Please judge clause 4.7.3.1(c) only. Everything else as it should be.

cards.title: Handrails on both sides, one interrupted
changes: The stair has handrails on ==both sides==.
One handrail is continuous throughout the stair and its landings.
The other handrail is ==interrupted== by a gap of 200 mm halfway along the flight.
cards.hint: Please judge clause 4.7.3.1(c) only. Everything else as it should be.

cards.title: Bollard on a ramp
cards.prompt: A bollard stands on a ramp, not on a level floor. From where should its height be measured for clause 4.2.3.6(c)?

options.label: From the ramp surface directly under the bollard
options.detail: At the centre of its base.

options.label: From the lowest point of the ramp surface around the bollard
From the highest point of the ramp surface around the bollard
From the finished floor level of the storey

cards.title: Kerb ramp in a drop-off area
cards.prompt: Where an accessible drop-off area has no kerb ramp, the clear distance of 4.2.3.6(a) is checked for all its bollards. How should a check decide whether a drop-off area has a kerb ramp?

options.label: A kerb-ramp element lies inside or touches the drop-off area
A stated property of the drop-off area
options.detail: Please name it in the note.

options.label: A person decides from the drawings

cards.title: Bollard in a drop-off area
cards.prompt: When does a bollard count as standing in an accessible drop-off area for clause 4.2.3.6(a)?

options.label: When it lies inside the drop-off area
options.detail: Its footprint fully within the area.

options.label: When it touches or overlaps the drop-off area
When it lies within a stated distance of the drop-off area
options.detail: Please name the distance in the note.

closing.title: Finally
closing.free_text_label: Is there anything else in applying these two clauses that an automated check should settle explicitly? Any other remarks?
